2025 General Executive Summary for DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site.
5 Year Anniversary Resubmission & Revisions to the Plan

The October 20, 2020, plan is being submitted on October 1, 2025, for the following reasons:
	5-year anniversary resubmission.
Change Summary
	Legal entity, ownership properties and assets changes from DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC to Qnity (E&I) business.  In connection with this separation and alignment process, the Qnity assets at the Midland, MI site will be transferred effective on or around October 1, 2025. 
o	These properties and asset changes occurred within Dow Michigan Operations I-Park to include RMP substance Bromine.  As a result, the process material has been removed from the DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC plan.  
	Offsite impact changes to the toxic Anhydrous Hydrogen Chloride (AnHCl) alternate case release scenario.  This release scenario was re-evaluated using a more realistic release rate based on process knowledge of maximum operating pressure and line size.  This change resulted in an increase in the endpoint distance to 1.8 miles, which increased the population impacted.  No other impacts were noted because of this change.  Reported as one of the toxic alternate case scenarios.  
	Worst case reported scenario has changed since 2020 from CMME to AnHCl due to a safety project to improve the secondary containment for CMME which installed a deeper, smaller surface area trench to reduce the pool evaporation rate.  

(A) Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Sites overall approach to chemical safety is through adherence to state and federal regulations as well as corporate standards and requirements.  For continued compliance, the site conducts internal 1st party audits in addition to corporate 2nd party compliance audits.

DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site is strongly committed to employee, public and enviro

nmental safety.  This commitment is demonstrated by a comprehensive accidental release prevention program that covers areas such as design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training associated with the processes at the facility.  Appropriate controls are implemented to prevent possible releases of regulated substances.  If a release were to occur, highly trained emergency response personnel are on hand to control and mitigate the effects of the release.  The facility also coordinates with the City of Midland Fire Department and Midland LEPC, which can provide additional emergency response expertise.

(B) Description of the Stationary Source and Regulated Substances Handled
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site primary activity on the site is chemical manufacturing, including specialty products and chemicals, adhesives and plastics.  There are two (2) covered processes, two (2) programs and five (5) regulated substances present at DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC. Site stationary source.  

The regulated substances are listed below.  
Regulated Substances:
Anhydrous Hydrogen Chloride (HCl)
Chloromethyl methyl ether
Dimethylamine
Oleum (Fuming Sulfuric Acid)
Trimethylamine

(C) The General Accidental Release Prevention Program
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC site has taken all the necessary steps to comply with the accidental release prevention requirements set out under 40 CFR part 68 of the EPA.  This facility was designed and constructed in accordance with applicable company and governing agency requirements at the time of construction.  Modifications to existing structures are also made in compliance with applicable company standards and governing agency requirements.  Several processes at the facility are subject to the OSHA Process Safety Management standard under 19 CFR 1910.119.  The facility is also subject to EPCRA Section 302 notification requirements.  The following sections briefly describe the elem

ents of the release prevention program that is in place at the DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US Inc. Site.

Process Safety Information
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site maintains detailed records of safety information that, among other things, describe the chemical hazards, operating parameters and equipment design associated with all covered processes.  Numerous types of information are available to supplement safety information, including Safety Data Sheets for materials used on site, equipment and engineering design specifications and applicable reactive chemicals testing.

Process Hazard Analysis
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site conducts comprehensive studies to ensure that hazards associated with the processes are identified and controlled efficiently.  For initial screening and risk evaluation, Reactive Chemical screening and Process Hazard Analysis are conducted.  These methodologies are supplemented when needed with analyses that may include:  What-if Analysis, Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Layers of Protection Analysis (LOPA), Fault Tree Analysis and Safer Technology and Alternative Analysis (STAA).  A team of qualified personnel performs the studies along with experts in engineering and process operations.  Any findings related to the hazard analyses are addressed in a timely manner and/or put into the corporate event and action tool for compliance tracking.

Operating Procedures
For safely conducting activities within the covered processes, DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site maintains written operating procedures.  These procedures address various modes of operation such as initial startup, normal operations, temporary operations, emergency shutdown, emergency operations, normal shutdown and startup after a turnaround.  The information is regularly reviewed and is readily accessible to operators involved in the processes.

Training
DDP Specialty Electronic Materi

als US LLC Site has a comprehensive training program in place to ensure that employees who are operating processes are competent in the operating procedures associated with these processes.  Refresher training is provided at least every three years and more frequently as needed.

Mechanical Integrity
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site carries out documented maintenance inspections on process equipment to ensure proper operations.  Process equipment examined by these inspections includes pressure vessels, storage tanks, piping systems, relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown and safety systems, instrument controls and pumps.  Maintenance operations are carried out by qualified personnel with training in maintenance practices.  Furthermore, these personnel receive specialized training as needed.  Any equipment deficiencies identified by the maintenance checks are corrected in a safe and timely manner.

Management of Change
Written procedures are in place at the DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site to manage changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment and procedures.  Process operators, maintenance personnel or any other employee whose job tasks are affected by a modification in process conditions are promptly made aware of and receive training on the modification.

Pre-startup Reviews
Pre-startup safety reviews related to new processes and to modifications of existing processes are conducted as regular practice at the DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site.  These reviews are conducted to confirm that construction, equipment and operating & maintenance procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing equipment into operation.

Compliance Audits
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site conducts audits on a regular basis to determine whether the provisions set out under the RMP rule and other applicable regulatory requirements are being followed and have been implemented properly.  Audits are conducted using an es

tablished schedule for the site.  Corrective actions required because the audits are undertaken in a safe and prompt manner.

Incident Investigation
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site promptly investigates any incident that has resulted in or could reasonably result in the release of a regulated substance.  These investigations are undertaken to identify the root causes leading to the incident as well as any corrective actions to prevent the release from recurring.  The facility also investigates minor and near-miss incidents as a preventive measure.

Employee Participation
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site operates on the premise that process safety management and accident prevention is a team effort.  Company employees are encouraged to express their views concerning accident prevention issues, to attend applicable reviews, and to recommend improvements.  Improvements are solicited and implemented as appropriate.  In addition, employees have access to all information created as part of the facility's implementation of the RMP rule, including information resulting from process hazard analyses.

Contractors
On occasion, the DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site hires contractors to conduct specialized maintenance, construction and various other activities.  Prior to selecting a contractor, a thorough evaluation of safety performance of the contractor is carried out.  The facility has a strict program for informing contractors of known potential hazards related to the contractor's work and the processes, as well as the procedures for emergency response should an accidental release of a regulated substance occur.  Contractors are also required to inform the facility of any hazards they may introduce or encounter while at the site.

(D) Five-year Accident History
The DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site has not had any accidental releases from any of the covered processes resulting in deaths, injuries or significant property

damage on or off site in the previous five years.  

(E) Emergency Response Plan
DDP Specialty Electronic Materials US LLC Site utilizes Dow Emergency Services and Security (ES&S) within the MiOps I-Park who maintains a Site written Emergency Response Plan to deal with accidental releases of hazardous materials and to respond to emergencies both internally and externally.  The Emergency Planning Committee within MiOps has the responsibility to oversee changes to the Site Emergency Plan.  Committee members consist of I-Park tenants to include Site Emergency Managers, members from all On-Call groups, Emergency Services and Security along with Midland Site Responsible Care Leaders.  

Each business unit within MiOps is required to maintain their individual written plan to meet all the legal and regulatory requirements regarding emergency preparedness. The plan documents all aspects of emergency response including adequate first aid and medical treatment, evacuations, notification of local emergency response agencies and the public, and post-incident decontamination of affected areas.  The plan is updated as necessary to reflect any pertinent changes within the processes at the facility that would require a modified emergency response.

The facility works with the Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC) with which the facility emergency plan has been coordinated and verified.

At least one Site and/or Community Emergency Training Exercises are conducted annually by Dow ES&S.  All I-Park business units are required to participate in the Site Emergency Training Exercises.  Each business unit is responsible for evaluating hypothetical information and determining whether it affects their location and subsequently uses the exercise to gain learning value in preparing for a real time event.
